statement: Let r<1 and q be C1 on [r,1), with q(r)=r, qprime(r)<=1, q<=1 and qprime strictly convex on (r,1). Then q(t)<t for r<t<1. A crossing forces qprime(t)>1 by strict trapezoid comparison; subsequent convex secants force q(s)>1 near 1. No derivative at one is used.

label: Square-root terminal deficit on a finite plateau
statement: For gamma in U with gamma=c on (a,1), where 0<=a<1 and finite c>=0, and its controlled diffusion, there are C>0 and t0<1 such that 1-q(t)>=C*sqrt(1-t) for t0<t<1. statement: For the admissible zero coefficient in pure zero-field SK, q0(t)=2 arcsin(t)/pi and D+P(0)[1]=1/4-1/pi<0. Thus empty Stieltjes support cannot occur at a minimizer. The calculation does not inherit minimizer moment identities.

label: Strict increase on a zero constant interval
statement: For gamma in U and its controlled diffusion, if gamma=0 on an open interval I contained in (0,1), then q''(t)=E[Phi_xxx(t,X_t)^2]>0 for t in I; thus q' is strictly increasing there. A Gaussian transition from any earlier interior time gives full spatial support. Phi_xxx cannot vanish identically, because an even quadratic cannot be both one-Lipschitz and a bounded distance from |x|.
